rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act - Grounds for Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant only for good cause as specified by statute, including failure to pay rent, disorderly conduct, damage to property, substantial violation of lease rules, breach of lease covenants, and failure to pay rent increase after notice.
rules.summary_plain: In New Jersey, a landlord can only evict you for specific reasons like not paying rent, causing damage, or breaking lease rules, and must follow legal procedures.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, un propietario solo puede desalojarte por razones específicas como no pagar el alquiler, causar daños o romper las reglas del contrato, y debe seguir procedimientos legales.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartments, rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, hotels, motels, or transient/seasonal guests renting less than 120 days, or units held in trust for developmentally disabled family members.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.
